about.title: West Sacramento Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision changes everything, and the days that follow are often overwhelming. In 2025, Yolo County recorded six traffic deaths alongside hundreds of injury collisions, many along corridors like US-50, I-80, West Capitol Avenue, and Jefferson Boulevard, with Friday evening hours between 5 and 7 p.m. seeing the heaviest reported activity. California law allows a spouse, domestic partner, or children to pursue a wrongful death claim first, followed by certain dependents or heirs if none exist. LawProactive is not a law firm — we're a free service that connects West Sacramento families with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened, explain the two-year filing deadline, and walk through what losses may be recoverable. You focus on your family; we help you find someone who can focus on the legal path forward.

whyChoose.title: Why West Sacramento Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Standing Rules Can Be Confusing
items.desc: California limits who may bring a wrongful death claim, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children before other dependents or heirs. An attorney can help clarify where your family stands.

items.title: The Two-Year Clock Is Firm
items.desc: Wrongful death claims generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window can be shorter if a government entity was involved, such as a city road issue. Missing it can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. An attorney can help explain how these losses apply to your specific situation.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Typically a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none exist, certain other dependents or heirs may have standing. An independent attorney can review your family's situation and confirm who qualifies.

items.question: Is a wrongful death case connected to any criminal charges against the driver?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal prosecution. Even if criminal charges are filed, dropped, or never pursued, a family may still bring a civil claim. The two proceedings operate independently and follow different rules.

items.question: Does it matter that the crash happened near a busy West Sacramento corridor like I-80 or US-50?
items.answer: Public crash records show these corridors, along with Jefferson Boulevard and West Capitol Avenue, account for a meaningful share of reported collisions in the area, particularly during Friday evening hours. An attorney can look at the specific circumstances of your loss and how the location and timing may factor into the case.

items.question: What if my loved one was partly involved in causing the collision?
items.answer: California follows a comparative fault system, so a family may still pursue a claim even if the deceased shared some responsibility. Any recovery could be adjusted based on the degree of fault. An independent attorney can walk through how this might apply to your circumstances.
